text.en: The fricative /s/ in Ainu belongs to a single phoneme, with *sh* being a slightly palatalized variant of *s* ⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--s-and-sh-belong-to-the-same-phoneme⟧. It is realized as [ʃ] before [i] and in syllable-final position, and as [s] elsewhere ⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--the-fricative-s-is-realized-as-either-s⟧. More specifically, /s/ palatalizes to [ʃ] before /i/, and syllable-final /-s/ is often palatalized unless followed by a word beginning with [s] ⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--refsing-s-palatalization-conditioning⟧. For Sakhalin Ainu, Murasaki states the distribution categorically: /s/ is pronounced [ʃ] in syllable-final position and in the syllable /si/, and [s] in all other positions ⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--s-is-pronounced-syllable-finally-and-in-the⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語の摩擦音/s/は単一の音素に属し、*sh*は*s*が少し口蓋化した変異体にすぎない⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--s-and-sh-belong-to-the-same-phoneme⟧。/s/は[i]の前および音節末の位置では[ʃ]として実現され、それ以外の位置では[s]として実現される⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--the-fricative-s-is-realized-as-either-s⟧。より詳しくは、/s/は/i/の前で[ʃ]に口蓋化し、音節末の/-s/は[s]で始まる語が後続しない限りしばしば口蓋化する⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--refsing-s-palatalization-conditioning⟧。樺太アイヌ語については、村崎が明確に記述しており、/s/は音節末および音節/si/において[ʃ]と発音され、それ以外の位置では[s]と発音される⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--s-is-pronounced-syllable-finally-and-in-the⟧。

text.en: When /s/ occurs at the onset of a syllable before *i*, the sequence *si* is pronounced [ʃi], rendered in Japanese as 'シ', rather than [si], which would correspond to 'スィ' ⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--the-sequence-si-is-pronounced-i-rather-than⟧.
text.ja: 音節頭において/s/が*i*の前に現れる場合、*si*という連続は[ʃi]、すなわち日本語の「シ」として発音され、[si]すなわち「スィ」のような音とはならない⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--the-sequence-si-is-pronounced-i-rather-than⟧。

text.en: Syllable-final *s* resembles the initial sound of Japanese 'shi' ([ɕ]), though it can also be pronounced close to [s] ⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--syllable-final-s-resembles-the-initial-sound-of⟧. In Chitose Ainu, Bugaeva reports that /s/ is as a rule not palatalized unless it is preceded or followed by /i/ ⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--in-chitose-ainu-s-is-as-a-rule⟧.
text.ja: 音節末の*s*は日本語の「し」の頭音に似ているが、[s]に近く発音されることもある⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--syllable-final-s-resembles-the-initial-sound-of⟧。千歳アイヌ語においては、Bugaevaによれば、/s/は/i/に先行されるか後続されない限り、原則として口蓋化しない⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--in-chitose-ainu-s-is-as-a-rule⟧。

text.en: The pronunciation of *si* in Ainu is identical to Japanese [ɕi] ('shi') and is not a [si]-like sound ⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--the-pronunciation-of-si-in-ainu-is-identical⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語における*si*の発音は日本語の「し」([ɕi])と同じであり、「スィ」のような[si]に近い音ではない⟦claim:phon/s-palatalization--the-pronunciation-of-si-in-ainu-is-identical⟧。
